Hi Alyssa — thanks, we can absolutely provide the detail. Attached is our proposed implementation roadmap (PDF) and a network checklist for your infra team. Key points below; please flag anything you want expanded into the doc.

High-level timeline (recommended, 8-week plan):
- Week 0: Procurement + NDA + SAML metadata exchange and account provisioning
- Week 1: Network enablement (IP allowlist, egress rules), service endpoints validation
- Week 2: Test integration: SDK/auth smoke tests, sample requests, rate-limit baselining
- Week 3: Data prep & migration dry-run (export, transform, embed-loading into private deployment)
- Week 4: Canary rollout (1% of production traffic or ~5k requests/day) with logs/tracing enabled
- Week 5: Observe & tune (2 full business cycles), expand to 10% if stable
- Week 6: Scale to 50% with autoscaling policies enabled and quota adjustments
- Week 7: Full cutover weekend; rollback plan and post-cutover validation

Integration steps (concise):
1) Exchange SAML metadata (IdP + SP) and test SSO in staging
2) TLS and certificate validation for private endpoints
3) Configure prefix/KV caching options; plan for cache warm-up during canary (estimated 12–24 hours for significant history)
4) Migrate historical embeddings in batches; use parallel workers to limit latency impact
5) Set up tracing hooks and per-route dashboards in Redwood Console

Canary & rollback criteria:
- Canary size: start at 1% (configurable), increase to 10% after 72 hours if: 99th-pctl latency <= 2x baseline AND error rate < 0.1%
- Rollback triggers: sustained error rate > 0.5% for 30m, data-corruption detection, or SLA-critical latency spikes

Dependencies & compliance asks:
- SOC 2 report (we can share the latest SOC 2 Type II SOC pack once an NDA is in place)
- SSO metadata and test accounts for SSO validation
- Network allowlist windows during cutover (we recommend a 3-hour maintenance window for full-data sync)

I've kept the timeline conservative to allow for procurement/IT scheduling; if you have a preferred blackout weekend we can align. Documents attached: redwood-implementation-roadmap-v1.pdf, helios-network-checklist.xlsx, cutover-runbook-templates.md

Thanks — I copied Rishi (SE) and Marissa (CS) who will own technical validation and success metrics.

Regards,
Jordan Blake

Redwood Inference

Hi Alyssa — adding CS input on success criteria and runbook ops. Thanks for the clear ask.

Success metrics (what we'll monitor during canary and ramp):
- Latency: mean and 95th/99th percentiles per model and per route (alert at 99th > 2x baseline)
- Cost: tokens per successful request and estimated monthly delta at projected traffic 
- Accuracy/regression: set of 50 smoke prompts from your product team for regression monitoring
- Error rates and model fallback frequency

Canary ops & support model:
- Canary sample size: start 1% for 72 hours; success -> 10% for 5 business days -> 50% for 2 business days -> full cutover
- Rollback: automated routing fallback to the previous model version + disable autoscale (manual confirmation required)
- Support: 24/5 on-call for cutover weekend; runbook will include exact escalation tree and play-by-play checklist

Ask: please confirm the preferred cutover weekend (we suggest June 12–13) and provide the list of internal stakeholders who must be on the 3-hour maintenance call. Once we have that, Jordan/Rishi and I will produce a final signed runbook and SOC2 access matrix for procurement.

Thanks,
